text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German debt markets had a choppy session on Tuesday, digesting domestic employment and industry orders data, warily eyeing the direction of U.S. Treasuries and witnessing a credit tightening in Britain. Although Bunds and futures prices were wallowing in soft ground in late trade, players said domestic fundamentals should continue to support German markets for the time being. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.84, up 0.29 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts locked in a dramatic 2-9/32 gain on Tuesday, the biggest one-day rally for five years, after a 1/4 percent rise in interest rates, but have little upside potential left, traders said. "I don't think there is much money to be made in gilts in the short-term," one senior treasury trader said.
The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-13/32, up 2-9/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and interest rate futures settled little changed on Tuesday after a relatively quiet session with traders viewing the latest polls showing a narrowing of the gap between the left and right with caution.
The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.46, down 0.04. from Monday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian Btp bond futures ended firmer, helped by particularly by Bonds and supported by hopes of a near-term cut in the Bank of Italy's key discount rate.
The June Liffe Btp contract ended 99 basis points higher at 128.83 after touching a session high of 128.94, with the next test seen at 129.00/05.
The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.75 up 0.91 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities prices were lower as players were anxious ahead of the Treasury's sale of $17 billion of three-year notes. The government will sell three-year notes this session and $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday. The new supply made some players nervous the Wall Street community would be able to absorb it efficiently. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-30/32, down 3/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.91 percent.
JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended down by more than a full point on Tuesday, as massive selling was triggered by a surge in Tokyo share prices.
The sudden rise in share prices led to speculation that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates earlier than expected and this weakened sentiment, dealers said.
In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.38, down 0.92 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market was a bit more active on Tuesday than it was last week, but supply was capped by a forthcoming European holiday on Thursday and in anticipation of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.
